meta.notes: Three weeks up and down the California coast finishing in Las Vegas. Fog in the mornings up north, desert heat down south — pack layers and sun cream. This whole plan works offline once installed, so don't panic when the signal drops in Big Sur or Death Valley.

legs.title: San Francisco
legs.tagline: Fog, hills and sourdough — easing in on the bay.
legs.notes: Four nights at Hotel Julian to shake off the jet lag. Mornings are foggy and cool right through August (Karl the Fog is real), so keep a layer in every bag even when it looks sunny. Parking is brutal — lean on cable cars, ferries and walking.

ideas.title: Alcatraz Island
ideas.note: Former island prison — the audio tour narrated by ex-guards and inmates is gripping. Pre-book, it sells out.

ideas.title: Ride a cable car
ideas.note: The Powell-Hyde line climbs past the Lombard Street zig-zags — hang off the side.

ideas.title: Fisherman's Wharf & Pier 39
ideas.note: The barking sea lions on the docks are a hit with the little ones. Skip the seafood stalls — plenty else to eat here.

ideas.title: Musée Mécanique
ideas.note: A free museum of working antique arcade machines at Fisherman’s Wharf — bring a pocket of quarters and let the kids play. One of the largest collections of its kind in the world.

ideas.title: Painted Ladies, Alamo Square
ideas.note: The Full House row of Victorian houses — a quick photo stop with a park to run around in.

ideas.title: Chinatown
ideas.note: The oldest Chinatown in the US. Watch fortune cookies being folded on Ross Alley.

ideas.title: Walk or cycle the Golden Gate Bridge
ideas.note: Ride over to the harbour town of Sausalito, then ferry back with the bikes.

ideas.title: Muir Woods
ideas.note: Towering old-growth redwoods 30 mins north. Cool and shaded — good for a hot day. Book parking ahead.

ideas.title: Twin Peaks at sunset
ideas.note: The best panorama of the whole city and bay. Bring a layer — it gets windy and cold up top.

ideas.title: Exploratorium
ideas.note: Hands-on science playground on the waterfront — brilliant for the younger ones, and the teens get sucked in too.

ideas.title: California Academy of Sciences
ideas.note: Rainforest dome, planetarium and aquarium under a living roof. A whole rainy-morning in one.

ideas.title: Walt Disney Family Museum
ideas.note: In the Presidio — the story of Walt Disney, with early sketches and models. A nice warm-up for Disneyland later.

ideas.title: Mission District murals
ideas.note: Balmy and Clarion Alleys are packed with street art — a good wander for the teens with a camera.

ideas.title: Koret Children's Quarter, Golden Gate Park
ideas.note: The oldest public playground in the US, with a restored 1914 carousel. Perfect to burn off the little ones' energy.

ideas.title: Yerba Buena Gardens & carousel
ideas.note: Downtown lawns with a historic carousel and the kid-focused Children’s Creativity Museum next door.

ideas.title: SF Giants baseball at Oracle Park
ideas.note: Check if the Giants are home. A waterfront ballpark right on the bay — a proper American night out.

ideas.title: In-N-Out Burger, Fisherman’s Wharf
ideas.note: The West Coast burger institution. Ask for it "animal style". No seafood in sight.

ideas.title: Tony's Pizza Napoletana, North Beach
ideas.note: Award-winning pizza in the Italian quarter — a crowd-pleaser for all six.

ideas.title: Ghirardelli Square sundaes
ideas.note: Hot-fudge sundaes at the old chocolate factory — the little ones will not forget it.

ideas.title: Mission-style burrito, La Taqueria
ideas.note: The definitive giant SF burrito. Cheap, filling and easy for fussy eaters.

days.title: Arrival in San Francisco
days.subtitle: Wheels down — a gentle first evening by the water.

options.title: Check in & Fisherman's Wharf
options.plan: Land at SFO, collect the rental car and check in to Hotel Julian. Once bags are dropped, take a slow stroll to Pier 39 to see the sea lions — the perfect low-effort way to stay awake and beat the jet lag. Early night for everyone.
options.food: A hearty sourdough bread bowl (chilli or broccoli-cheddar — skip the chowder) at Boudin Bakery on the Wharf.

options.title: Ferry Building sunset
options.plan: If everyone's wired rather than wiped, wander the Embarcadero to the Ferry Building marketplace and watch the light go down over the Bay Bridge.
options.food: Tacos or a slice from the Ferry Building food hall, eaten by the water.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Have all six passports and the car-hire confirmation ready at the rental desk, and confirm the twins' booster seats before you drive off.

days.title: Alcatraz & the waterfront
days.subtitle: The Rock — history the kids will actually remember.

options.title: Alcatraz cruise & cellhouse tour
options.plan: Ferry out to Alcatraz for the excellent self-guided audio tour narrated by former guards and inmates — genuinely gripping for teens and 9-year-olds alike. Give it a good 2.5 hours on the island, then ferry back. Booked: the 1:05pm City Cruises ferry from Pier 33 (ref GYGX7M9G9XWQ) — arrive 30 mins early.
options.food: Lunch at the Ferry Building on the way back — build-your-own from the stalls.

options.title: The Exploratorium
options.plan: If Alcatraz is sold out (book it well ahead), Pier 15's Exploratorium is a giant hands-on science playground — hours of fun and air-conditioned.
options.food: The Seaglass café on-site, or back to the Wharf.

tip.label: Booked — 1:05pm
tip.body: Alcatraz is booked for the 1:05pm ferry from Pier 33 (not the Wharf), ref GYGX7M9G9XWQ. Arrive 30 minutes early; mornings are foggy so bring a layer.

days.title: Golden Gate & the bay
days.subtitle: The postcard day — bridge, bikes and Sausalito.

options.title: Cycle the bridge to Sausalito
options.plan: Hire bikes near the Wharf and ride the waterfront path across the Golden Gate Bridge to the pretty harbour town of Sausalito, then let the ferry carry you — and the bikes — back to the city.
options.food: Burgers and wood-fired pizza with a marina view at Barrel House Tavern, Sausalito.

options.title: Presidio & Baker Beach
options.plan: Drive to the Presidio, walk the Batteries-to-Bluffs trail and take the classic bridge photo from Baker Beach. Tunnel Tops park is superb for the twins.
options.food: Picnic from the Presidio Tunnel Tops kiosks or the Sessions food trucks.

options.title: Cable car & Lombard Street
options.plan: Ride the Powell-Hyde cable car up to Lombard Street's famous zig-zag, then down to Ghirardelli Square.
options.food: A hot fudge sundae at Ghirardelli — split a few, they're enormous.

tip.label: Layers
tip.body: The bridge is 10°C colder and windier than downtown, even in August. Everyone takes a jumper — no exceptions.

days.title: Muir Woods & last of the city
days.subtitle: Giant redwoods, then pack for the coast road.

options.title: Muir Woods, then city classics
options.plan: Drive over the bridge to Muir Woods and walk the boardwalk loop beneath 1,000-year-old redwoods. Back in the city, tick off the Painted Ladies at Alamo Square and a Twin Peaks sunset before repacking for tomorrow's drive.
options.food: Picnic at Muir Beach (or the cosy Pelican Inn), then a Mission burrito for dinner.

options.title: Golden Gate Park & the Academy
options.plan: Stay in town: the California Academy of Sciences (aquarium, planetarium, rainforest) plus the Japanese Tea Garden and Stow Lake pedal-boats.
options.food: The Academy café, or picnic by the park bandshell.

tip.label: Prep the drive
tip.body: Pack tonight, fuel up, and download offline maps for Monterey → Big Sur — signal disappears on the coast road tomorrow. This app already works offline.

legs.title: Pacific Coast Highway
legs.tagline: The drive is the destination — Big Sur, cliffs and Hearst Castle.
legs.notes: Two days threading Highway 1 south. Night 1 in Cambria (Hampton Inn San Simeon), night 2 in Santa Monica (Days Inn). Phone signal is patchy to non-existent through Big Sur — screenshot anything you need, and trust this app, which runs fully offline. Fill the tank whenever it drops below half.

ideas.title: 17-Mile Drive
ideas.note: Scenic toll road past the Lone Cypress and Pebble Beach. Slow, beautiful, lots of pull-offs.

ideas.title: Bixby Creek Bridge
ideas.note: The iconic Big Sur arch bridge — pull into the viewpoint just north for the classic shot.

ideas.title: McWay Falls
ideas.note: An 80ft waterfall dropping onto a hidden beach. Short easy walk from the car park.

ideas.title: Pfeiffer Beach
ideas.note: Purple-tinged sand and a keyhole rock arch. The access lane is narrow and easy to miss.

ideas.title: Point Lobos Reserve
ideas.note: Coves, sea otters and easy cliff trails — the "crown jewel" of the state parks.

ideas.title: Elephant seal rookery, Piedras Blancas
ideas.note: Hundreds of elephant seals hauled out yards from a free boardwalk. A guaranteed wildlife win for the kids.

ideas.title: Morro Bay
ideas.note: A giant volcanic plug rising out of the bay — a good leg-stretch and ice-cream stop.

ideas.title: Cannery Row, Monterey
ideas.note: The Steinbeck-famous waterfront strip — sweet shops, an old carousel and the aquarium at the end.

ideas.title: Hearst Castle
ideas.note: The over-the-top hilltop mansion of a newspaper tycoon. Pre-book the timed tour bus from the visitor centre.

ideas.title: Monterey Bay Aquarium
ideas.note: World-class aquarium — the kelp forest and touch pools are a firm favourite with younger ones. Dated tickets are cheaper.

ideas.title: Dennis the Menace Park, Monterey
ideas.note: A wildly creative playground (real train engine, big slides) designed by the Dennis the Menace cartoonist. A perfect PCH break for the little ones.

ideas.title: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
ideas.note: A classic seaside amusement park with a wooden roller coaster — if the route takes you through Santa Cruz.

ideas.title: Lunch at Nepenthe
ideas.note: Cliff-top Big Sur restaurant with jaw-dropping views. Order the famous Ambrosia burger — no seafood needed.

stays.name: Days Inn by Wyndham Santa Monica
stays.address: 3007 Santa Monica Blvd, Santa Monica, CA 90404

days.title: San Francisco → Big Sur → Cambria
days.subtitle: The big one — cliffs, bridges and hidden beaches.

options.title: The Big Sur coast road to Cambria
options.plan: Leave the city and drive Highway 1 south — the signature day of the trip. Loop the 17-Mile Drive, stop at Bixby Creek Bridge, walk to the McWay Falls overlook, and detour to purple-sanded Pfeiffer Beach. Drive slowly, stop often; overnight in Cambria (Hampton Inn San Simeon).
options.food: Nepenthe for lunch — famous cliff-top terrace a thousand feet above the Pacific. Book or arrive early.

options.title: Break at Monterey
options.plan: Split the drive with a couple of hours at the world-class Monterey Bay Aquarium and a stroll along Cannery Row before pushing into Big Sur.
options.food: Wood-fired pizza or burgers in Monterey — try Alvarado Street Brewery.

tip.label: No signal
tip.body: There is essentially zero reception through Big Sur — screenshot directions and fuel up in Monterey (one very pricey station on the whole stretch). This page works with no connection at all; watch for fog on the cliff bends.

days.title: Cambria → Hearst Castle → Santa Monica
days.subtitle: Castles, elephant seals, then down to the beach.

options.title: Hearst Castle & the drive south
options.plan: From San Simeon, take the tour bus up to Hearst Castle — the jaw-dropping hilltop mansion — then stop at the Piedras Blancas rookery where hundreds of elephant seals lounge on the beach. Afterwards, the long, scenic run down via Santa Barbara to Santa Monica (Days Inn tonight).
options.food: Lunch on Stearns Wharf or at the Public Market in Santa Barbara.

options.title: Morro Bay & the Rock
options.plan: Skip the castle tour for laid-back Morro Bay, dominated by its 176m volcanic rock — kayak the bay or just watch the otters — then drive on down.
options.food: Fish tacos on the Morro Bay Embarcadero.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Hearst Castle tours must be pre-booked and depart on a strict timetable from the visitor centre. Aim to clear Santa Barbara by mid-afternoon so the last stretch into Santa Monica stays sane.

legs.title: Santa Monica
legs.tagline: Beach base — pier lights, bikes and Pacific sunsets.
legs.notes: Two nights at the Hampton Inn & Suites, walkable to the beach. The classic beach path runs all the way from Santa Monica to Venice — hire cruiser bikes and use it. The car can mostly stay put.

ideas.title: Santa Monica Pier & Pacific Park
ideas.note: The end of Route 66 — a small amusement park with a Ferris wheel and coaster right over the ocean.

ideas.title: Cycle the beach path to Venice
ideas.note: Hire cruiser bikes and ride the flat 3-mile path along the sand to Venice and back.

ideas.title: Beginner surf lesson
ideas.note: Gentle Santa Monica breakers and lots of schools — a fun morning for the teens to try.

ideas.title: Venice Beach boardwalk & Muscle Beach
ideas.note: Street performers, skate park and the famous outdoor gym. Busy, colourful and free.

ideas.title: Venice Canals
ideas.note: A quiet, pretty grid of canals and footbridges just off the boardwalk — a lovely stroll.

ideas.title: Malibu beaches (El Matador)
ideas.note: Sea caves and rock arches a short drive up the coast. Steep steps down, so wear proper shoes.

ideas.title: Getty Villa
ideas.note: A recreated Roman villa full of antiquities above the Malibu coast. Free entry, timed ticket needed.

ideas.title: Tongva Park playground
ideas.note: A modern park right by the pier with fountains and climbing frames — easy to let the little ones loose.

ideas.title: Abbot Kinney Boulevard
ideas.note: Hip Venice street of boutiques, murals and coffee — good for a teen mooch.

ideas.title: Third Street Promenade
ideas.note: Pedestrianised shopping street with street performers — easy walk from the beach.

ideas.title: Original Farmers Market & The Grove
ideas.note: Historic food stalls (tacos, BBQ, bakeries — no seafood required) next to an open-air shopping street with a trolley.

ideas.title: Bay Cities Italian Deli
ideas.note: Home of "the Godmother" sub — the best sandwich in LA. Grab them for a beach picnic.

ideas.title: Salt & Straw ice cream, Abbot Kinney
ideas.note: Cult small-batch ice cream with wild flavours. A guaranteed hit with the kids.

days.title: Santa Monica Pier & beach
days.subtitle: Roller coaster over the ocean.

options.title: Pacific Park & a proper beach day
options.plan: Move to the Hampton Inn & Suites, then a full beach day. Ride the solar-powered Ferris wheel and coaster at Pacific Park on the pier, hire umbrellas and bodyboards, and let the twins loose in the sand. Sunset over the Pacific from the pier is the reward.
options.food: Burgers and shakes at a pier-side spot.

options.title: Bike the beach path to Venice
options.plan: Hire cruiser bikes and ride the flat 3.5km beach path south to Venice and back, stopping wherever looks good.
options.food: Poke bowls or tacos on the Venice side.

tip.label: Beach kit
tip.body: Rent beach cruisers for the whole family for the two days — it turns the coast into your back garden.

days.title: Venice & Malibu
days.subtitle: Canals, murals and hidden coves.

options.title: Canals, Abbot Kinney & Malibu beaches
options.plan: Morning at the peaceful Venice Canals and the boutiques and murals of Abbot Kinney, with a look at the boardwalk chaos. In the afternoon, drive up the coast to Malibu's beautiful state beaches — El Matador's sea caves and arches are the showstopper.
options.food: Abbot Kinney for lunch, fish tacos at a Malibu beach shack for later.

options.title: Family surf lesson
options.plan: Book a group beginner surf lesson on the mellow Santa Monica or Venice breaks — instructors are used to kids and everyone stands up eventually.
options.food: Well-earned brunch on Main Street, Santa Monica.

tip.label: Parking
tip.body: El Matador's car park is tiny and fills by late morning — go early, and pack water as there are no shops at the beach.

legs.title: Los Angeles
legs.tagline: Hollywood, theme parks and the big-city stretch.
legs.notes: Seven nights at the SpringHill Suites (Burbank/Downtown) — your big base for the week. LA is vast and the traffic is real; plan each day around one area and travel outside peak hours. Burbank is handy for Universal, Warner Bros and Griffith. This is the leg where the four kids' tastes pull hardest, so a couple of days split the group.

ideas.title: Hollywood Walk of Fame & TCL Chinese Theatre
ideas.note: The stars and the hand-prints in the forecourt. Busy and a bit gritty — go early.

ideas.title: Griffith Observatory
ideas.note: Free observatory with the best Hollywood Sign view and evening telescopes. Stunning at sunset.

ideas.title: Universal Studios Hollywood
ideas.note: Theme park + working studio backlot tram. The Wizarding World and Mario Land are the headliners. Consider Express in August.

ideas.title: Disneyland / California Adventure
ideas.note: The original Disneyland. Needs a dated ticket AND a park reservation — sort both ahead and set up Genie+.

ideas.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
ideas.note: The coaster capital — record-breaking thrill rides. The teens’ day; not for the little ones.

ideas.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour
ideas.note: Ride through the backlot and sound stages (Friends, DC). Right by the Burbank hotel. Great for film-mad teens.

ideas.title: The Broad
ideas.note: Free contemporary art museum downtown — the Infinity Mirror Rooms need a timed reservation.

ideas.title: La Brea Tar Pits
ideas.note: Ice-age fossils bubbling out of tar in the middle of the city. The mammoths are a winner for younger kids.

ideas.title: Natural History Museum
ideas.note: Dinosaurs, gems and a butterfly pavilion — a solid all-ages half-day, and cool indoors when it’s hot.

ideas.title: Getty Center
ideas.note: Hilltop art museum reached by a little tram, with gardens and huge city views. Free entry.

ideas.title: Griffith Park & LA Zoo
ideas.note: One of the largest urban parks in the US — the zoo, trails and picnic lawns keep all ages happy.

ideas.title: Travel Town & pony rides, Griffith Park
ideas.note: A free outdoor train museum with a miniature railroad to ride, plus nearby pony rides — made for the little ones.

ideas.title: Rodeo Drive & Beverly Hills
ideas.note: The famous luxury shopping street — fun to window-shop and spot the odd celebrity.

ideas.title: LA Dodgers at Dodger Stadium
ideas.note: Check if the Dodgers are home. An iconic ballpark in the hills — grab a Dodger Dog.

ideas.title: Porto's Bakery, Burbank
ideas.note: Beloved Cuban bakery minutes from the hotel — cheese rolls and potato balls for pennies. Perfect breakfast run.

ideas.title: Pink's Hot Dogs, Hollywood
ideas.note: An LA institution since 1939 — chilli dogs with a queue to match. Cash-friendly and kid-proof.

ideas.title: Grand Central Market, DTLA
ideas.note: A buzzing food hall — tacos, burgers, egg sandwiches and more. Something for every fussy eater, no seafood needed.

stays.name: SpringHill Suites LA Burbank/Downtown
stays.address: 549 S San Fernando Blvd, Burbank, CA 91502

days.title: Santa Monica → LA (Burbank)
days.subtitle: Move to base, then the best view in the city.

options.title: Move to Burbank & Griffith sunset
options.plan: Drive across to the SpringHill Suites — your base for the week — and settle in. Late afternoon, head up to Griffith Observatory for the best free view in LA, a superb space museum, and the definitive Hollywood Sign photo as the sun drops.
options.food: In-N-Out for the full American road-trip experience, or dinner in Los Feliz below the observatory.

options.title: The Getty Center
options.plan: Prefer a slower move-in day? Ride the tram up to the Getty for world-class art, gardens and one of the best views over LA — free to enter.
options.food: The Getty's restaurant and café, with a view.

tip.label: Beat the crowds
tip.body: Griffith Observatory parking fills fast at sunset — arrive well before golden hour or use the DASH shuttle, and bring a layer for after dark.

days.title: Universal Studios Hollywood
days.subtitle: Movie-world day — and it's right by Burbank.

options.title: Universal Studios Hollywood
options.plan: A big day at Universal: the Studio Tour tram through real backlots, the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Super Nintendo World and Jurassic World. Something for the 9s, the teens and the grown-ups. Get there for opening.
options.food: Eat inside the park — Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade is the fun choice.

options.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour
options.plan: For film-mad teens, the Warner Bros. tour in nearby Burbank goes behind the scenes of real working sets and prop houses.
options.food: Lunch on the studio lot or in Burbank.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Buy dated Universal tickets online and consider the Express pass — August queues are long. Rope-drop the Studio Tour first.

days.title: Hollywood
days.subtitle: Stars on the pavement, sign on the hill.

options.title: Walk of Fame & the sights
options.plan: Do the Walk of Fame and the handprints at the TCL Chinese Theatre, mooch Hollywood Boulevard, and take in the Dolby/Ovation complex. An easy, iconic day at a gentle pace after two big park days.
options.food: Dinner in Los Feliz, or the classic In-N-Out.

options.title: The Broad & Downtown
options.plan: For the older four, The Broad downtown (Yayoi Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms are the draw) plus the striking Walt Disney Concert Hall next door.
options.food: Grand Central Market — dozens of food stalls under one roof.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: The Broad is free but timed-entry tickets go fast, and the Infinity Rooms need a separate reservation — sort it a few days ahead.

days.title: Disneyland
days.subtitle: The big one for the twins.

options.title: Disneyland Park, Anaheim
options.plan: A full day at the original Disneyland (about an hour south). Rope-drop the headliners (Rise of the Resistance, Space Mountain, Indiana Jones), pace it with breaks, and stay for the fireworks over the castle.
options.food: Eat in the park; a Dole Whip in Adventureland is an easy win.

options.title: Disney California Adventure
options.plan: The sister park across the plaza — Avengers Campus, Cars Land and the Guardians drop tower skew a bit older, so it can suit the teens better.
options.food: Pym Test Kitchen in Avengers Campus is a laugh.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Disneyland needs a dated ticket AND a park reservation. Download the app and set up Lightning Lane / Genie+ the night before to skip the worst queues.

days.title: Griffith Park & museums
days.subtitle: A gentler recovery day after Disney.

options.title: LA Zoo & Griffith Park
options.plan: A deliberately easier day. The LA Zoo and the vintage Travel Town train museum in Griffith Park are perfect for tired twins, with plenty of shade and space to roam.
options.food: Picnic in Griffith Park, or a casual lunch in Los Feliz.

options.title: La Brea Tar Pits
options.plan: Bubbling Ice Age tar pits and a museum full of sabre-tooth cats and mammoths, right in the middle of the city — a quirky, kid-friendly winner.
options.food: The Original Farmers Market at 3rd & Fairfax is a short hop.

options.title: Back to the beach
options.plan: Fancy the coast again? An easy day back at Santa Monica or Venice beach — no driving stress, just sand and the pier.
options.food: Whatever takes your fancy on the pier or Abbot Kinney.

tip.label: Split if you like
tip.body: A good day to split by energy — quiet zoo/park for the twins, museums or the beach for the older ones.

days.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
days.subtitle: The teenagers' day — serious coasters.

options.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
options.plan: Aimed squarely at the 15- and 17-year-olds: Magic Mountain (up near Valencia) has one of the biggest roller-coaster line-ups on the planet. A great day to split the group — thrill-seekers here, twins and a grown-up to a pool or the beach.
options.food: Park food, or refuel in Valencia on the way back.

options.title: Pool & beach day
options.plan: The other half takes it easy — hotel pool in the morning, Santa Monica beach in the afternoon. Everyone reconvenes for dinner and swaps stories.
options.food: Family dinner back near Burbank — somewhere everyone's voted for.

tip.label: Split the group
tip.body: Height limits keep the twins off most of Magic Mountain's big rides, so splitting the day is kinder to everyone. Agree a pickup time and place before you separate.

days.title: Getty, Beverly Hills & desert prep
days.subtitle: Culture, glamour, and stocking up for Nevada.

options.title: The Getty & a Beverly Hills stroll
options.plan: Ride the tram up to the Getty Center for art, gardens and views, then a stroll down Rodeo Drive for the Beverly Hills people-watching. A cooler, calmer last LA day — and the chance to stock the car before the desert.
options.food: Lunch at the Getty, or a deli in Beverly Hills.

options.title: Farmers Market & The Grove
options.plan: The Original Farmers Market and the open-air Grove for a relaxed food-and-shopping morning before the drive.
options.food: Take your pick of the Farmers Market stalls.

tip.label: Desert prep
tip.body: Buy a case of water and check the car's air-con works properly before tomorrow — you're driving into serious August heat. Charge everything tonight.

legs.title: Las Vegas
legs.tagline: Neon, desert wonders and one last blow-out.
legs.notes: Seven nights to finish — one at the W Las Vegas (23–24), then the Luxor (24–29). August in Nevada is brutally hot (40°C+): plan outdoor stuff for early and late, hide from the midday sun in the air-conditioned casinos and pools, and hydrate constantly. The Grand Canyon and Death Valley pages work with no signal at all.

ideas.title: The Strip after dark
ideas.note: Walk the neon between the mega-resorts — the Bellagio fountains, the Venetian and the fake landmarks. Free and dazzling.

ideas.title: High Roller observation wheel
ideas.note: The giant Ferris wheel at The LINQ — a 30-min ride with the best view over the valley, best at dusk.

ideas.title: Seven Magic Mountains
ideas.note: Towers of neon-painted boulders in the desert 20 mins south — a fun, free photo stop.

ideas.title: Hoover Dam
ideas.note: An engineering marvel 45 mins out. Walk across into Arizona; the dam tour is worth the ticket.

ideas.title: Grand Canyon West / Skywalk
ideas.note: The nearest rim to Vegas (2.5 hrs), with the glass Skywalk out over the canyon. Book the West Rim package ahead.

ideas.title: Red Rock Canyon
ideas.note: A 13-mile scenic loop of red sandstone cliffs 30 mins from the Strip — easy short walks. Go early before the heat.

ideas.title: Death Valley
ideas.note: The hottest place on earth, 2 hrs west. Extreme in August — only for a very early, well-prepared day trip.

ideas.title: Gondola ride at The Venetian
ideas.note: A singing gondolier poles you round the indoor canals — kitsch, air-conditioned and the little ones love it.

ideas.title: Adventuredome at Circus Circus
ideas.note: A huge indoor theme park — roller coasters and rides with no desert heat. Great mid-afternoon escape.

ideas.title: Shark Reef Aquarium, Mandalay Bay
ideas.note: A walk-through aquarium with a shark tunnel — cool, dark and a sure thing for the younger ones.

ideas.title: Discovery Children's Museum
ideas.note: Three floors of hands-on play downtown — the perfect air-conditioned morning for the little ones.

ideas.title: The Mob Museum
ideas.note: The story of organised crime in a former courthouse — surprisingly gripping for teens and grown-ups.

ideas.title: Fremont Street Experience
ideas.note: Old downtown Vegas under a giant LED canopy — free light shows, buskers and a zipline overhead.

ideas.title: A family show
ideas.note: A Cirque du Soleil show (Mystère / "O") or a magic act — plenty are all-ages. Book ahead for good seats.

ideas.title: Hershey’s & M&M’s World
ideas.note: Multi-floor chocolate megastores on the Strip — a sugar-fuelled treat and free air-con.

ideas.title: Bacchanal Buffet, Caesars
ideas.note: The blow-out Vegas buffet — carving stations, pizza, dumplings and desserts. Skip the raw bar and there’s no seafood in it.

ideas.title: In-N-Out Burger, Las Vegas
ideas.note: The reliable, cheap, no-seafood family favourite when you just want a proper burger.

ideas.title: Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium
ideas.note: Check the August fixtures. The spectacular "Death Star" stadium just off the Strip — a bucket-list NFL night.

stays.name: W Las Vegas
stays.address: 3940 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89119

stays.name: Luxor Hotel & Casino
stays.address: 3900 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89119

days.title: Los Angeles → Las Vegas
days.subtitle: Across the Mojave into Nevada.

options.title: Drive to Vegas & the Strip by night
options.plan: The roughly 4.5-hour drive across the Mojave to Las Vegas — break it at the tiny outpost of Baker (home of the world's tallest thermometer). Check in to the W Las Vegas, cool off, then hit the Strip after dark for the Bellagio fountains and the neon.
options.food: One of the famous Vegas buffets, or an easy Strip diner — the kids will be wide-eyed either way.

options.title: Death Valley crossing
options.plan: For the adventurous: route via Death Valley National Park — Badwater Basin (lowest point in North America), Zabriskie Point and the dunes. Spectacular, but only with a fully fuelled, well-watered car.
options.food: Stock up before you enter — services inside the park are minimal and far apart.

tip.label: No signal
tip.body: Fuel up and load the car with water before leaving LA. Long stretches have no reception and 45°C+ heat — this page works fully offline. Never leave anyone in a parked car.

days.title: The Strip
days.subtitle: Family-friendly Vegas, believe it or not.

options.title: High Roller, fountains & Adventuredome
options.plan: Move to the Luxor (your base for the rest of the trip), then a family Strip day: ride the High Roller wheel, gawp at the Bellagio fountains and the Venetian's gondolas, raid M&M's World, and burn off energy at Circus Circus's indoor Adventuredome.
options.food: The Venetian's food hall or a Strip pizzeria keeps everyone happy.

options.title: Pool day
options.plan: It's 40°C+ — sometimes the answer is the Luxor pool all day, then the Strip in the cool of the evening.
options.food: Poolside snacks, then a proper dinner out once the sun's down.

tip.label: Heat plan
tip.body: Do the outdoor Strip early morning or after sunset; take the middle of the day indoors. Refill water bottles everywhere and slap on the sun cream.

days.title: Grand Canyon West
days.subtitle: One of the great wonders — worth the early start.

options.title: Grand Canyon West day trip
options.plan: The big finale excursion. Grand Canyon West (about 2.5 hours out) is the closest rim, home of the glass Skywalk jutting over the void, plus Eagle Point and Guano Point. Set off at dawn to be back for the evening.
options.food: Lunch at the Grand Canyon West ranch, or pack a hamper for the drive.

options.title: Hoover Dam & Lake Mead
options.plan: Prefer a shorter day? The colossal Hoover Dam is only 45 minutes out — walk across the dam, cross the bypass bridge, and add a Lake Mead viewpoint.
options.food: Lunch in Boulder City, the town that built the dam.

tip.label: Early start
tip.body: A long day in the heat — leave before sunrise, take far more water than you think you need, and keep an eye on the kids near the largely unfenced rim edges.

days.title: Beat the heat & old Vegas
days.subtitle: A lazy day, then the neon of Fremont Street.

options.title: Pool day + Fremont Street by night
options.plan: A well-earned lazy day at the Luxor pool after the canyon, then head to old-town Fremont Street after dark for the canopy light show, buskers and the zipline overhead — the original, gaudy heart of Vegas.
options.food: A classic Fremont Street steakhouse or the food hall.

options.title: Adventuredome & indoor Strip
options.plan: Dodge the peak heat entirely — the indoor Adventuredome theme park, the giant sweet shops, and the air-conditioned casino spectacles.
options.food: Grab a table at one of the themed Strip restaurants.

tip.label: Heat plan
tip.body: Peak desert heat is midday — save everything outdoor for after sunset, and keep the water going.

days.title: Hoover Dam & Lake Mead
days.subtitle: Engineering marvel in the desert.

options.title: Hoover Dam & the bypass bridge
options.plan: Drive out to the colossal Hoover Dam (45 min) — walk across the dam, take the power-plant tour, and cross the bridge for the classic view. Add a Lake Mead viewpoint on the way back.
options.food: Lunch in Boulder City, the sweet little town that built the dam.

options.title: Red Rock Canyon loop
options.plan: Swap the dam for the scenic 13-mile loop drive through the red sandstone of Red Rock Canyon, 30 minutes the other side of the Strip.
options.food: Picnic at a Red Rock overlook, or back to the Strip.

tip.label: Early start
tip.body: Go early to beat both the heat and the coach tours; the dam car park fills up fast.

days.title: Last full day
days.subtitle: One more Vegas night to remember.

options.title: A show + Strip favourites
options.plan: Tick off any Strip must-dos you've missed, then a family-friendly Cirque du Soleil production or a big magic show for the final night — a proper send-off.
options.food: A blow-out final dinner somewhere everyone's been eyeing up.

options.title: Seven Magic Mountains + pool
options.plan: A quieter last day: the giant neon Seven Magic Mountains boulders (20 min south) for photos, then the pool and packing.
options.food: Poolside, then dinner on the Strip.

tip.label: Book ahead
tip.body: Popular shows sell out — book earlier in the week. Pack tonight; it's a travel day tomorrow.

days.title: Departure — flying home
days.subtitle: Three weeks done. Wheels up from Las Vegas.

options.title: Last breakfast, return the car, fly home
options.plan: A relaxed final morning: pack, one last American breakfast, top up the fuel and return the rental car, then to Harry Reid International (LAS) in good time for the flight home. Sleep on the plane — it's an overnight back to the UK.
options.food: A final proper American breakfast — pancakes, bacon and unlimited coffee.

options.title: Seven Magic Mountains photo
options.plan: If the flight's later, the Seven Magic Mountains — a stack of giant neon-painted boulders 20 minutes south — make a fun, quick final photo before the airport.
options.food: Grab-and-go coffee and pastries on the way to the airport.

tip.label: Don't miss the flight
tip.body: Return the hire car with a full tank to avoid the refuelling surcharge, and leave a big buffer — LAS security queues are long. Passports, ESTAs and boarding passes ready before you leave the hotel.

bookings.name: Flights — LHR → San Francisco / Las Vegas → LHR
bookings.note: Six seats. Open-jaw: fly into SFO, home from LAS. Confirm seat allocation for the family together.

bookings.name: ESTA visa waivers ×6
bookings.note: One per traveller including the twins. Apply at least 72 hours before flying; print or screenshot the approvals.

bookings.name: Rental car — 7-seater SUV
bookings.note: 22-day hire, SFO pickup / LAS drop-off (one-way fee applies). Two booster seats for the twins.

bookings.name: Travel insurance — family policy
bookings.note: Full family cover including the theme-park and Grand Canyon activities and US medical.

bookings.note: Timed reservation mandatory — no turn-ups. Book the parking or the shuttle in advance.

bookings.name: Hearst Castle tour

bookings.note: 13–14 Aug (1 night).

bookings.name: Universal Studios Hollywood tickets
bookings.note: Dated tickets; consider the Express pass for August crowds.

bookings.name: SpringHill Suites LA Burbank/Downtown

bookings.name: Disneyland tickets + park reservation
bookings.note: Needs BOTH a dated ticket and a park reservation. Set up Genie+ the night before.

bookings.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain tickets
bookings.note: Buy online in advance; the teens' day.

bookings.name: W Las Vegas
bookings.note: 23–24 Aug (1 night).

bookings.name: Luxor Hotel & Casino
bookings.note: 24–29 Aug (5 nights).

bookings.name: Grand Canyon West day tour
bookings.note: Book the Skywalk / West Rim package and confirm the pickup or self-drive parking.

bookings.name: Las Vegas Raiders tickets
bookings.note: NFL game at Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas — check the August fixtures fall within our Vegas dates (23–29 Aug) and book seats together.

packing.name: Passports & ESTA printouts
packing.note: All six, plus the car-hire and hotel confirmations. Keep together in one folder.

packing.name: Sun cream (high SPF) & hats
packing.note: Reef-safe, factor 50. The desert and the beach will both catch you out.

packing.name: Layers for the fog
packing.note: San Francisco and Big Sur are cold and windy even in August. A fleece and a light waterproof each.

packing.name: Reusable water bottles ×6
packing.note: Essential for the desert legs — refill everywhere. One each, labelled.

packing.name: US plug adapters & power bank
packing.note: UK→US adapters (a couple of multi-port ones), plus a power bank for the no-signal drives.

packing.name: Phone chargers & car charger
packing.note: Everyone's cable, plus a multi-port car charger for the long driving days.

packing.name: Swimwear & beach towels
packing.note: Quick-dry towels save space. Goggles for the pools and the sea.

packing.name: Comfortable walking shoes
packing.note: Broken-in trainers each — theme parks and canyon rims mean big step counts.

packing.name: Kids' entertainment
packing.note: Downloaded films, games and audiobooks for the flights and the long drives — offline, no signal needed.

packing.name: Medications & first-aid kit
packing.note: Any prescriptions in hand luggage, plus plasters, antihistamines, ibuprofen and travel-sickness tablets for the coast road.
